questions.question: A shopkeeper gains 20% when he sells an article at a 20% discount on its marked price. If the cost price of the article is reduced by 20% and he wants to earn a profit of 26%, then how much per cent discount should he give on the same marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be Rs 100

Selling price = Rs 100 - Rs 20 = Rs 80

Cost price = 80over 120 × 100 = 200over 3

New cost price = 200over 3 × 80over 100 = 160over 3

Selling price for 26% profit = 126over 100 × 160over 3 = Rs 67.2

Discount needed = Rs 100 - Rs 67.2 = Rs 32.8

Discount % = 32.8over 100 × 100 = 32.8%

∴ **Total discount needed would be 32.8%.**

questions.question: If the 9-digit number 45069x4y8 is divisible by 44, then what is the value of (x - 2y) for the minimum value of y?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

9-digit number 45069x4y8 is divisible by 44

Concept:

The divisibility rule of 4 states that for a number to be divisible by 4, its last two-digit should be perfectly divisible by 4.

The divisibility rule of 11 states that for a number to be divisible by 11, the difference between the sum of odd and even digits should be either completely divisible by 11 or zero. 

Calculations:

Using the Divisibility rule of 4, we get-

∴ y8 is completely divisible by 4 if y is 0. (Taking the minimum value of y)

Similarly using divisibility rule of 11, we get-

⇒ (4 + 0 + 9 + 4 + 8) - (5 + 6 + x + 0) = 25 - (11 + x) = 14 - x

⇒ The number is perfectly divisible if x = 3 (∴ x = 3)

∴ value of (x - 2y) = (3 - 2 × 0) = 3

The value of (x - 2y) is 3.

questions.question: A tyre has 3 punctures. The first puncture alone would have made the tyre flat in 14 minutes, the second alone would have done it in 28 minutes, the third alone would have done it in 56 minutes. If air leaks out at a constant rate, how long (in minutes) does it take for all the punctures together to make the tyre flat?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by 1st puncture to flat the tyre = 14 min

Time taken by 2nd puncture to flat the tyre = 28 min

Time taken by 3rd puncture to flat the tyre = 56 min

**Formula:**

Efficiency = Total time taken ÷ time taken by individual punctures

**Calculation:**

Taking LCM of 14, 28, and 56 = 56

Let the total time taken to flat the tyre = 56 min

Efficiency of puncture 1 = 56 / 14 = 4

Efficiency of puncture 2 = 56 / 28 = 2

Efficiency of puncture 3 = 56 / 56 = 1

Total efficiency = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7

Total time taken if air leaks out through all three puncture = 56over 7 = 8 min

∴ **The tire would flat out in 8 minutes.**

questions.question: P and Q travel a distance of 120 km such that the speed of P is faster than Q. The sum of their speeds is 75 km/h and together they took the total time of 6 hours and 40 minutes. Then the speed of Q (in km/h) is
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance travelled = 120 km

Sum of speeds of P and Q = 75 km/hr

Total time taken by both = 6 hours 40 min

**Concept used:**

Speed = distance /time

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a - b)² = a2 + b2 - 2ab

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of P be p km/hr and Q be q km/hr

q + p = 75 km/hr ----(i)

According to the question,

(120/p) + (120/q) = 6 hours and 40 minutes or 20/3 hours [As 1 hour = 60 minutes]

⇒ [(120q + 120p)/pq] = 20/3

⇒ 360q + 360p = 20pq ----(ii)

By multiplying eq (i) with 360 we get,

360q + 360p = 75 × 360

Now,

20pq = 75 × 360

⇒ pq = (75 × 360)/20

⇒ pq = 1350

Again,

(q + p)² = 5625

⇒ q² + p² + 2pq = 5625

⇒ q2 + p2 + 2pq - 4pq = 5625 - 4 × 1350

⇒ q2 + p2 - 2pq = 5625 - 5400

⇒ (q - p)² = 225

⇒ (q - p) = 15 ----(iii)

From eq (i) and eq (iii) we get

q = 30 and p = 45

So, speed of P is 45 km/h and Q is 30 km/h

**∴ The speed of Q (in km/h) is 30.**

For an equilateral triangle, the median, altitude, and angle bisector are the same. Hence, in ΔABC, AD is the median, altitude, and angle bisector for the ∠BAC.

⇒ ∠BAD = ∠DAC = 60ºover2 = 30º

⇒ ∠ADE = 75º

From the figure, ∠EDC = 90º - ∠ADE

⇒ ∠EDC = 90º - 75º = 15º 

∴ **The measure of ∠EDC is 15º.**

questions.question: The average runs scored by Sumit in the first 3 matches is 122. In the 4th match, he scored some runs such that his average runs now become 130. In the 5th match, he scored 14 less runs than those in the 4th match, and now the average of his last 4 matches becomes 164. The runs scored by Sumit in the 1st match is:
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Total runs = Average runs × number of matches

**Calculation:**

Total runs scored in the first three match = 3 × 122 = 366

Total runs scored in the first four match = 4 × 130 = 520

Run scored in the fourth match = 520 - 366 = 154

Run scored in the fifth match = 154 - 14 = 140

Total runs scored in five matches = 520 + 140 = 660

Total runs scored in the last fourth match = 164 × 4 = 656

Run scored in the first match = 660 - 656 = 4

∴ **Sumit scored 4 runs in the first match.**

A and B can do a certain work in 27 days and 36 days, respectively. A worked for a few days and then B joined him. They together worked till the completion of the work. If the work got completed in a total of 18 days, then for how many days did A and B work together?
questions.solution:
Given:

Days in which A can complete the work = 27 days

Days in which B can complete the work = 36 days

Days after which total work was completed = 18 days

Formula:

Efficiency = Total work / Time taken to complete work individually

Calculation:

LCM of 27, 36, 18 = 108

Assuming that the total work is 108 units.

Efficiency of A-

⇒ 108over 27 = 4 units of work/day

Efficiency of B-

⇒ 108over 36 = 3 unit of work/day

Total work done in 18 days by A working alone = 4 units × 18 = 72 units

Remaining work = 108 - 72 = 36 units

Time taken by B to complete 36 units of work = 36over 3 = 12 days

∴ **A and B worked for 12 days.**

questions.question: The ratio of acid and water in solutions A and B is 15 ∶ 11 and 4 ∶ 9, respectively. 6 litres of A is mixed with 4 litres of B. How much acid (in ml) should be added to 390 ml of the resulting solution so that the ratio of acid and water in it becomes 3 ∶ 2?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Acid in the solution A = 15 : 11

⇒ Quantity of acid in 6 liters of solution A = 15over 26 × 6 = 45over 13

Acid in the solution B = 4 : 9

⇒ Quantity of acid in 4 liters of solution B = 4over 13 × 4 = 16over 13

Total acid in 10 liters of A and B = 45over 13 + 16over 13 = 61over 13

Total acid content in 390 ml of such solution = 0.39 × {61over 13}over 10 = 183 ml

Total water content in 390 ml of such solution = 390 - 183 = 207 ml.

Let the acid to be added be "a"

According to the question-

⇒ 183 + aover 207 = 3over 2

⇒ 366 + 2a = 621

⇒ 2a = 621 - 366

⇒ 2a = 255 

⇒ a = 127.5 ml

∴ **The quantity of the acid to be added is 127.5 ml.**
